artifact.change_summary: Re-verified all v1.1 comparator leads by direct download/text-extraction rather than abstract or snippet; closed the B01, B02, B03, B04 coverage-insufficient gaps with newly retrieved, section-verified primary and/or independent sources; verified the corrected B06 original-method source (Heuer 1999 ch.8) by full-text retrieval; added two new comparator mechanisms (B07 concept/role separation; B08 double-loop learning) with section-verified primary sources.
artifact.limitations: B08 (double-loop learning) has a section-verified primary source but no section-verified independent second source was found within the time available; it is marked operational_coverage=partial rather than padded. Two PDFs (Harmsen 1997 thesis, NASA SE Handbook) are large documents; only the sections cited were read in full, not the entire document. The OntoClean source (KE02) is a book-chapter preprint hosted on the authors' own institutional site; exact final published page numbers (201-220 per the 2004 Handbook on Ontologies, Springer) were confirmed via a secondary bibliographic search, not by inspecting the published book itself.

records.title: An Analysis of the Requirements Traceability Problem
records.author: Orlena C. Z. Gotel and Anthony C. W. Finkelstein
records.identifier: Proceedings of the 1st IEEE International Conference on Requirements Engineering (ICRE'94), Colorado Springs, 18-22 April 1994, pp.94-101
relevant_sections: Section 5.1-5.2 Defining RT and Pre-RS/Post-RS traceability (pre-RS = life prior to inclusion in the Requirements Specification; post-RS = life after inclusion)
Section 6 Problems confronting pre-RS traceability (establish/end-use conflict, Figures 2-3)
Section 7 Solutions to pre-RS traceability problems
Section 8 Research agenda: location & accessibility of pre-RS sources as 'the crux of the problem'
records.paraphrase: Based on empirical study of 100+ practitioners, distinguishes pre-RS traceability (tracing a requirement back to its originating statements/actors, prior to specification) from post-RS traceability (tracing a baselined requirement forward through derived artifacts), and finds most reported traceability problems stem from inadequate pre-RS traceability, especially the inability to locate and access original sources/participants.
records.coverage: section-verified; full 8-page paper downloaded from the author's own institutional page (Pace University) and read in full, including all 9 numbered sections and reference list

records.title: Psychology of Intelligence Analysis, Chapter 8: Analysis of Competing Hypotheses
records.author: Richards J. Heuer, Jr.
records.identifier: Center for the Study of Intelligence, Central Intelligence Agency (book; no ISBN in original CSI printing)
relevant_sections: Chapter 8 'Analysis of Competing Hypotheses', pp.95-98, including the 8-step ACH procedure box and footnote 85 ('The analysis of competing hypotheses procedure was developed by the author...')
records.paraphrase: Presents an 8-step procedure (generate hypotheses via group brainstorming; list evidence/arguments per hypothesis; build a hypothesis-by-evidence matrix and assess diagnosticity; refine; draw tentative conclusions by trying to disprove rather than prove; test sensitivity to key evidence; report full likelihood ranking, not just the top hypothesis; identify future milestones/indicators) for comparing competing explanations by seeking disconfirming rather than confirming evidence.
records.coverage: section-verified; full 214-page PDF downloaded from the Internet Archive item 'PsychologyOfIntelligenceAnalysis' (filename Psychology_of_Intelligence.pdf, description confirms CIA Center for the Study of Intelligence, 1999) and text-extracted; footnote 85 in the chapter itself attributes authorship of the ACH procedure to Heuer

records.title: On the representation of roles in object-oriented and conceptual modelling
records.author: Friedrich Steimann
relevant_sections: Section 2 'What's in a role?' (pp.85-87): Guarino's ontological distinction between role and natural type by semantic rigidity and foundation, and a 15-item enumerated list of commonly attributed role properties
Section 4.1 Formal definition of the LODWICK role-oriented modelling language
records.paraphrase: Distinguishes a 'natural type' (semantically rigid: an individual cannot lose it without losing identity, e.g. Person) from a 'role' (founded on a relationship, lacks semantic rigidity, carries its own properties/behaviour, e.g. Student), and formalizes roles as a separate representational category from the objects/types that play them.
records.coverage: section-verified; full 24-page PDF downloaded from the author's institutional page (Fernuniversität Hagen) and text-extracted

records.title: An Overview of OntoClean
records.author: Nicola Guarino, Christopher A. Welty
records.identifier: doi:10.1007/978-3-540-24750-0_8 (in S. Staab & R. Studer, eds., Handbook on Ontologies, Springer, pp.201-220)

records.title: Double Loop Learning in Organizations
records.author: Chris Argyris
relevant_sections: pp.115-116: single-loop vs. double-loop learning defined via the thermostat analogy (single loop = correct within existing settings/goals; double loop = question whether the settings/goals themselves should change)
pp.117-118: 'Model I' assumptions and the four 'governing variables' that people's action-strategies are designed to protect
records.paraphrase: Defines organizational learning as error detection and correction; single-loop learning corrects action within existing goals/policies (like a thermostat), while double-loop learning also questions and can revise the underlying governing variables/policies themselves when errors recur.
records.coverage: section-verified; text is the verbatim copyrighted 1977 Harvard Business Review article (copyright notice and original page headers/footers present in the extracted text) accessed via a third-party-hosted PDF copy because the official hbr.org page is paywalled; content, page numbers (115-124), and copyright line were confirmed directly from the extracted text, not assumed

rejected_leads.reason: Invalid bibliographic attribution carried over from the v1.0/v1.1 registry. The identifier 'RAND P-8078' resolves to Bruce Hoffman's 2003 RAND paper 'Al Qaeda, Trends in Terrorism and Future Potentialities: An Assessment,' not to any Richards J. Heuer Jr. publication on Analysis of Competing Hypotheses. Independently re-confirmed in this pass by search; not used as evidence. The correct original-method source is DA03 (Heuer 1999, Psychology of Intelligence Analysis, Chapter 8), which was located and full-text verified this pass.

Attempted to locate the Heuer book hosted directly at a static cia.gov PDF path analogous to the Tradecraft Primer's URL pattern (e.g. https://www.cia.gov/resources/csi/static/Psychology-of-Intelligence-Analysis.pdf); this returned HTTP 404. The CIA's own books-monographs landing page (https://www.cia.gov/resources/csi/books-monographs/psychology-of-intelligence-analysis-2) returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch. Used the Internet Archive's hosted copy (item 'PsychologyOfIntelligenceAnalysis', described in the item's own metadata as 'Center for the Study of Intelligence, Central Intelligence Agency, 1999') instead; not a rejection of the source itself, only of the direct-CIA-URL access path.

A first candidate free mirror of Argyris (1977) at theisrm.org produced a PDF with zero extractable text (scanned image, no OCR layer); could not be section-verified from that copy. A second mirror (avannistelrooij.nl) had a genuine text layer and was used instead (recorded as OL01); both mirrors host the same 1977 HBR article, this is a note about extraction feasibility, not a rejection of the source.

The v1.1 registry treated Brinkkemper 1996 (abstract only) as B01's primary source. This pass found and full-text-verified a stronger, genuinely operational primary source (Harmsen 1997 doctoral dissertation, ME03) and an independent primary-application source (ME04); ME01 is retained only as background lineage, not as one of the two sources meeting the coverage gate.
